title: Unbounded RCU Grace Period Delay (Long-Running Reader Memory Leak)
pattern: Acquiring an RCU read-side lock (`rcu_read_lock()` or equivalent) and performing blocking, long-running, or unbounded synchronous computations before invoking unlock.
why_bad: In RCU-based garbage reclamation, old memory segments cannot be freed until all active read-side critical sections complete (the grace period) [20, 268]. A long-running or stalled reader thread delays the RCU grace period globally [20]. This prevents updaters from reclaiming retired data nodes, resulting in massive memory growth and eventually causing OOM exhaustion [20].
detection: Identify blocks enclosed in RCU read-side locks that perform complex parsing, synchronous nested loops, or blocking system/network calls.
fix: Keep RCU read-side critical sections as brief and lightweight as possible; execute heavy data processing outside the lock boundaries, or utilize segmented SRCU regions [20].
source: Paul E. McKenney, *Is Parallel Programming Hard?*, Chapter 9.5 (RCU) / passages [20, 268].
